text:
ana: Heads-up — quantized bring-up caused an unexpected MRR drop on the rerank MTEB-like suite. Baseline MRR 0.421 -> 0.389 after q4_0. I see the regression in CI and can reproduce locally.
chris: Can you paste the eval runner command and the model artifact hash?
nana: Sure, command I ran locally:
```
./eval_runner --suite rerank_mteb --model models/redwood-v2-q4_0 --topk 10 --seed 42 --out results.json
```
results.json snippet: `{ "mrr": 0.389, "ndcg@10": 0.602 }`
liam: Strange — quantization normally preserves score ordering. Are we doing any post-normalization or change in topk codepath for fast kernels?
nana: I checked. No preproc diffs. The quantized path uses `fast_dot` kernel returning float16 buffers that we cast back to float32. Logs show a different code path for topk: `stable_topk` vs `heap_topk`. There is a tiny tie-handling discrepancy.
maria: CI also flagged intermittent flakiness on topk tie cases earlier this month. Remember PR #310 changed how we call `np.argsort` in the aggregator. Could be related.
devon: We should make tie-breaking deterministic instead of relying on sort stability. Quick patch idea:
```python
# sort by rounded score then doc_id to break ties deterministically
indices = np.lexsort((doc_ids, np.round(scores, 6)))
```
That will prevent tiny fp jitter from changing ordering.
chris: +1. Also add a regression unit in the harness that runs a fixed-seed smoke test and compares MRR within an epsilon. CI should fail deterministically if ordering changes.
nana: I'll open a hotfix PR that includes: (1) deterministic lexsort tie-breaker in the rerank aggregator; (2) a `rerank-smoke` CI job that runs quantized and unquantized artifacts against a stored golden output (seeded).
ci-bot: flaky-test-detect: rerank-smoke failed twice on master in the last 24h — marking unstable. See https://ci/internal/runs/9823 for logs.
maria: Also check metric definition: our MRR implementation used to treat missing docs as ignored in the average vs previously we treated them as zero. That semantics change can shift aggregated MRR when candidate sets differ. We should standardize.
liam: Agreed — standardize to "per-query reciprocal rank with missing -> 0" and add explicit unit tests with small vectors to lock semantics.
nana: :thumbsup: I'll include 10 deterministic test vectors, update metrics.md, and wire the `rerank-smoke` job to run in staging before merge. Plan: PR today -> run smoke in staging -> merge if green.
devon: :shipit:
